beats.say: Each port solved one problem alone. Production needs all of them at once.
So now you build one system, and then you try to break it.
beats.label: The capstone
beats.head: Build it, then break it

beats.say: This port has two parts: the fleet on your laptop, and the same fleet on Google Cloud.
beats.label: Port 13 · Capstone

check.prompt: In the capstone, an intruder pod in another namespace calls the database. What stops it?
check.why: The namespace denies inbound traffic by default. Only the app has a rule that allows it.

beats.say: Tugboat with probes and autoscaling. A database with its own disk. And a scheduled job.
beats.label: The fleet

beats.say: Around them: a gateway, network policies, and least-privilege accounts.
beats.label: The guards

beats.say: Then the chaos drills. Delete a pod. Drain a node. Send an intruder.
beats.label: Chaos drills
beats.head: Break it and watch it heal

beats.say: Second: the same files, on a real cloud.
You push the image to a registry, and change two lines.
beats.label: What changes
beats.head: Push the image, change two lines

beats.say: The manifests stay the same. That is the point of Kubernetes.
beats.label: The point
beats.head: One API on every cluster

beats.say: Delete the cluster when you finish. A load balancer costs money every hour.
beats.label: Do not forget
beats.head: Clean up, or keep paying

beats.say: Every port in one namespace. Prove it with chaos. And the same files run anywhere.
beats.label: Capstone

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
